correctness.rationale: The convex projected diameter is attained by projected original vertices, so one maximizes six projected unit edge lengths. Those edges have directions (0,1,±1)/sqrt2 and permutations. Thus D/ell=sqrt(1-(min(x-y,y-z))²/2) for sorted absolute normal coordinates x>=y>=z. The bound 1=x²+y²+z² >= 5m² gives m<=1/sqrt5 with equality only at signed permutations of (2,1,0)/sqrt5. A signed/permutation fundamental spherical chamber has normalized area density 12/pi in (z,phi); imposing x-y>=r and y-z>=r yields the stated elementary angular integral up to z*=sqrt((1-2r²)/3)-r. Six great-circle small bands give upper tail 6sqrt2 sqrt(eps); uniform bivariate Taylor expansion of the shrinking chamber gives lower tail 150sqrt5/pi delta². Independent projected-vertex comparisons matched coordinate-gap formula for 2000 random directions. The unbounded exact CDF and endpoint limits follow from analytic geometry, not Monte Carlo.

value.rationale: Euclidean diameter is a basic geometric functional of an orthogonal shadow; its complete law and exact minimizers distinguish a discrete 12-plane minimum set from a great-circle maximum set, generating different quadratic and square-root endpoint exponents. This is a natural full geometric-probability distribution, with independently meaningful sharp endpoint behavior, rather than a generic numerical moment.

final_claim: For a regular tetrahedron of edge length ell, the Euclidean diameter D of its uniform random planar orthogonal shadow has support [3ell/sqrt(10),ell], an exact one-dimensional CDF integral over a signed-permutation spherical chamber, unique minimizing normal orbit, and lower/upper endpoint probabilities of orders delta² and sqrt(epsilon) with sharp constants 150sqrt(5)/pi and 6sqrt(2).
limitations: Regular three-dimensional tetrahedron, Haar-normal orthogonal plane projections only.
CDF is an exact quadrature; no elementary antiderivative or nonregular extension asserted.
